India's Q1 GDP Growth of 7.8% Sparks Debate on Calculation Methods

India's economy grew by 7.8% in the first quarter of the fiscal year, making it the fastest-growing major economy. This figure has been defended by the government, which rejected claims that the actual growth was as low as 2.6%. Officials stated that comparing nominal growth of 2.6% with the 7.8% GDP figure is misleading. Experts and some political figures have questioned the methodology used to arrive at the 7.8% figure, with one former finance secretary standing by his calculation of growth below 2.5% at current prices. The government's defense involved an analogy, stating that one should compare apples to apples. The growth data was discussed by officials at international forums, including at Nasdaq.
